# The covstructs7 package {#sec-covstructs7}

@sec-links describes how a constrained scalar is carried onto the real line by
a link function. A modelling toolkit meets constrained matrices as well: the
covariance of a multivariate response, the precision of a random effect, the
penalty matrix of a smooth term. This chapter presents the objects `covstructs7`
uses for them, and explains why they are a separate construction rather than a
matrix-valued link.

The mathematics of differentiating a function of a matrix with respect to a
parametrisation of that matrix is classical, and @magnus1999 is the standard
reference. The unconstrained parametrisations themselves come from
@pinheiro1996, whose paper is the origin of the log-Cholesky map used here,
and @pourahmadi2011 reviews the field.

@sec-covstruct-contract sets out what a structure is: a map from an
unconstrained vector to a symmetric matrix, the derivatives of that map, and
the four quantities a likelihood asks of the matrix it produces. It explains
why the Jacobian of such a map is not diagonal and why that single fact rules
out treating the construction as a link.

@sec-covstruct-families presents the families the package ships. The
log-Cholesky map is the general positive definite case, and its log-determinant
turns out to be linear in the free vector. The diagonal families are where
this package composes with `linkfunctions7` rather than competing with it. The
scaled fixed matrix is the case a penalty needs, and it is the reason the
package admits matrices that are not of full rank.

@sec-covstruct-rank is about those. A rank-deficient matrix is not a defect
here but the definition of a penalty, and the section explains what has to
change to accommodate one: the determinant becomes a pseudo-determinant, the
inverse becomes a solve restricted to the range, and the rank itself has to be
determined in a way that does not depend on the arithmetic that produced the
matrix.
